title: Captive and custom silicon outside the headline chip market: size of in-house chips (Apple, hyperscaler ASICs) and how each publisher counts them
why_it_matters: WSTS excludes captive production while Gartner counts Apple; custom AI accelerators are growing fast, so the gap between publishers and the true chip value in AI systems may be widening.
questions: How large is the value of in-house designed chips (Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Tesla) by year?
Which of these flows through a WSTS-reporting partner (e.g. Broadcom, Marvell) and which is bought directly from foundries?
How does Gartner value captive chips?
primary_sources: Broadcom and Marvell 10-K custom silicon disclosures

title: WSTS product-category time series before 2020 (discretes, opto, sensors, analog, micro, logic, memory, 1986-2019)
why_it_matters: The free WSTS dataset has regions only; product splits for earlier years are needed for the 1986-2026 product history and memory-cycle analysis.
questions: What were annual WSTS sales by product category for 1986-2019?
Are older WSTS spring releases (JEITA, SIA archives) available with prior-year actuals?
